name: Home Assistant
tagline: Self-hosted REST and WebSocket APIs for smart-home states, services, and automations
description: Home Assistant exposes a RESTful JSON API on the same host and port as its web frontend (documented default port 8123; Home Assistant OS 2026.8+ may default to 80 for OS installs). Endpoints under /api/ let you read entity states, call services (lights, switches, climate), fire events, fetch history and logbook data, render templates, and more. Authentication uses a long-lived access token as a Bearer header. A WebSocket API is also available for real-time updates. Fully free and open source on your own hardware—there is no central multi-tenant cloud API host.

auth.details: Long-lived access token via Authorization: Bearer TOKEN. Create under user Profile → Long-Lived Access Tokens (valid 10 years). OAuth2/IndieAuth also available for third-party apps.

pricing.free_tier_limits: Unlimited on self-hosted instance (open source). No paid API metering. Optional Nabu Casa Cloud (~$6.50/mo US) is separate and not required for local API access.
pricing.paid_plans: Optional Nabu Casa Cloud: $6.50/mo or $65/yr (US) for remote access/voice; core local REST/WebSocket API remains free

use_cases: get current state of a light, sensor, or switch entity
turn on or off lights and switches via service calls
list all entity states on a Home Assistant instance
push external sensor readings into Home Assistant as entity states
pull entity history or logbook entries for a time range
call climate, cover, or media_player services from scripts
